subject: Algerian crude dataset
magnitude: WAT 267.85 to 299.05 K (mean 283.78, SD 5.76); density 0.7144 to 0.8432 g/cm3; wax 0.61 to 6.39 wt%; pour point 237.15 to 284.15 K; freezing point 235.55 to 286.35 K
conditions: 59 Algerian crudes, WAT by rotational pour point tester (torque slope change)
citation: Benamara, C., Gharbi, K., Nait Amar, M., Hamada, B. (2020). Prediction of Wax Appearance Temperature Using Artificial Intelligent Techniques. Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering, 45, 1319-1330.
notes: Freezing point is close to pour point in these data (within a few K).

subject: MLP-LMA model
magnitude: best model MLP-LMA overall AARD 0.2312 pct; GEP AARD 0.5484 pct
conditions: 59 Algerian crudes
citation: Benamara, C., Gharbi, K., Nait Amar, M., Hamada, B. (2020). Prediction of Wax Appearance Temperature Using Artificial Intelligent Techniques. Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering, 45, 1319-1330.
notes: AARD on a Kelvin scale; 0.55 pct of 284 K is about 1.6 K.

subject: GEP explicit WDT correlation
conditions: comprehensive experimental WDT database (size not seen); equation itself not read
citation: Nait Amar, M., Zeraibi, N., Benamara, C., Djema, H., Saifi, R., Gareche, M. (2024). Modeling wax disappearance temperature using robust white-box machine learning. Fuel, 376, 132703.
notes: Explicit GEP formula exists in the paper but the PDF was blocked (robots rule on repository, paywall at Elsevier).

subject: measurement method
magnitude: cloud point differences between techniques up to about 20 K
conditions: literature comparison of DSC, CPM, viscometry, light transmission, filter plugging on crude oils
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Daridon, J.-L. (2005). The limitations of the cloud point measurement techniques and the influence of the oil composition on its detection. Petroleum Science and Technology, 23(9-10), 1113-1128.
notes: Table 2 layout was scrambled in the copy; mean method pair differences 0.1 to 15 K.

subject: WAT vs WDT
magnitude: WDT minus WAT about 15 K by DSC and about 10 K by microscopy
conditions: attributed mainly to supercooling at high cooling rates
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Daridon, J.-L. (2005). The limitations of the cloud point measurement techniques and the influence of the oil composition on its detection. Petroleum Science and Technology, 23(9-10), 1113-1128.

subject: viscometry detection limit
magnitude: 2.5 pct viscosity deviation corresponds to about 1 wt% precipitated solids
conditions: Einstein relation eta = eta_f(1 + 2.5 phi) used to relate viscosity rise to solids
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Daridon, J.-L. (2005). The limitations of the cloud point measurement techniques and the influence of the oil composition on its detection. Petroleum Science and Technology, 23(9-10), 1113-1128.
notes: So viscometric WAT lags true thermodynamic WAT; the lag is larger for oils with a long paraffin tail.

subject: n-paraffin decay ratio Cn+1/Cn
magnitude: decay ratio 0.9 boundary: below it the heaviest paraffin mainly sets the cloud point; above it the heavy tail changes the whole precipitation curve; refined products about 0.5
conditions: simulated oils with Mw 230, 15 wt% wax, heaviest paraffin C50 or C90
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Daridon, J.-L. (2005). The limitations of the cloud point measurement techniques and the influence of the oil composition on its detection. Petroleum Science and Technology, 23(9-10), 1113-1128.
notes: Useful for synthetic n-paraffin distributions: exponential decay with ratio 0.88 to 0.92 for crudes.

subject: loss of paraffins above C50 (about 1 wt%)
magnitude: removing about 1 wt% of paraffins heavier than C50 changes simulated cloud point noticeably while mass change is within experimental error
conditions: simulated Oil A to Oil E
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Daridon, J.-L. (2005). The limitations of the cloud point measurement techniques and the influence of the oil composition on its detection. Petroleum Science and Technology, 23(9-10), 1113-1128.
notes: Magnitude of the WAT shift is shown in a figure, not read.

subject: n-paraffin decay ratio alpha = w(Cn)/w(Cn-1)
magnitude: default alpha 0.88 in the wax model of a commercial downhole fluid characterisation method
conditions: live oil wax model used to predict thermodynamic WAT locus
citation: Zuo, J.Y., et al. (2011). Methods and apparatus for characterization of petroleum fluid and applications thereof. US Patent 7,920,970 B2 (Schlumberger).
notes: Matches the 0.88 to 0.92 range used by Coutinho and Daridon 2005 for crude oils; a ready prior for synthetic n-paraffin distributions.

subject: WDT minus WAT
magnitude: WDT usually more than 10 C above WAT
conditions: Chinese waxy crudes, review
citation: Li, H., Zhang, J. (2002). The influence of the wax on the crude rheology. Oil and Gas Storage and Transportation, 21(11), 6-12.
notes: In Chinese; read via the English and Chinese abstract page.

subject: precipitated wax at pour point
magnitude: pour point reached at about 1 wt% precipitated wax; about 2 wt% precipitated wax gels the oil
conditions: Chinese waxy crudes, review
citation: Li, H., Zhang, J. (2002). The influence of the wax on the crude rheology. Oil and Gas Storage and Transportation, 21(11), 6-12.
notes: Key physical link for a generator: pour point is the temperature where the cumulative precipitated wax curve (from WAT downward) reaches about 1 to 2 wt%, so (WAT - pour point) shrinks as total wax content grows.

subject: gel point (Chinese standard) vs pour point (ASTM D97)
magnitude: linear relation from 84 paired measurements; not a fixed 3 C offset as commonly assumed
conditions: Chinese waxy crudes, SY/T 0541 gel point vs D97 pour point
citation: Chen, J., Zhang, J. (2005). The relationship between gel point and pour point of waxy crude. Oil and Gas Storage and Transportation, 24(8), 22-24.
notes: Coefficients in the PDF were font-garbled and could not be read; R2 near 0.99. Worth opening in a browser to convert Chinese gel point data to pour point.

subject: crude oil wax content classes
magnitude: wax free below 0.5; very low 0.5-3; low 3-5; moderate 5-10; high 10-20; very high 20-35 wt%
conditions: classification scheme quoted in a thesis on Kuwaiti crude blending
citation: Al-Besharah, J.M. (1989). The effect of blending on selected physical properties of crude oils and their products. PhD thesis, Aston University.
notes: Useful prior bands for sampling wax content.

subject: log(wax content)
magnitude: best single predictor of cloud point, pour point and CFPP of diesel blends was log(wax content); standard error within 3.5 C
conditions: 8 Bombay High refinery streams blended 24 ways; wax by Engler-Holde; linear model Y = A0 + A1 X1 + A2 X2 with X from n-paraffin >C15, chain length, wax content, T50
citation: Krishna, H., Bhattacharjee, S., Joshi, G.C., Singh, H., Purohit, R.C., Dhawan, S.V.K., Singh, K.K. (1989). Correlation of low temperature properties of diesel fuel with composition. Erdol und Kohle, Erdgas, Petrochemie (1989), 72-75.
notes: Table III coefficients unreadable in the OCR. Supports a log(wax) term in WAT and pour point models.

subject: pour point blending
magnitude: binary blend (0.687 SR gas oil at -6 F, 0.313 HT heavy gas oil at 40 F) has pour point about 15 F by the PPBI chart vs 8.4 F by linear average
conditions: pour point blending index chart method
citation: Penn State FSC 432 Petroleum Refining course notes, Lesson 9 Pour Point Blending.
notes: Blend pour point is about 7 F above the linear average; a check case for any power-law blending rule.

subject: blending ratio of waxy Shengli crude with a lighter oil
magnitude: WAT linear in blend ratio (R2 0.996): 51 C at 100 pct Shengli to 40 C at 50 pct, about 0.22 C per pct; wax content also linear (14.5 to 8.4 wt%, R2 0.984); pour point near linear (24 to 10 C after 80 C heat treatment)
conditions: 5 blends, DSC WAT; Shengli crude density 897.5 kg/m3 at 20 C
citation: Han, Z., Ma, L., Li, X., Zhu, H., Li, W., Xia, X., Zhang, X., Guo, R. (2024). Determination of wax deposition rate model of blended oils with different blending ratios. Processes, 12(4), 772.
notes: Supports a linear (volume or mass fraction) mixing rule for WAT and wax content when generating synthetic blends; pour point also roughly linear here, unlike distillate blends where it is pulled to the waxier part. WAT minus pour point stays about 27 to 30 C across blends.

subject: pour point
magnitude: pour point was the most influential input (feature selection) for WAT; best LSSVM R2 0.9893, AARD 9 pct on 81 points
conditions: 81 literature points: density 0.71-0.89 g/cm3, wax 0.61-25.78 wt%, pour point -36 to 37 C
citation: Kouhi, M.M., Shafiei, A., Bekkuzhina, T., Abutalip, M. (2025). New intelligent models for predicting wax appearance temperature using experimental data: flow assurance implications. Fuel, 380, 133146.
notes: Black-box models only; no explicit equation. AARD 9 pct is on a Celsius scale, so not comparable to Kelvin-scale AARDs of Benamara.

subject: paraffin content
magnitude: Kazakh fields: paraffin 2.1 to 21.1 wt% with saturation temperature 16.7 to 56 C (Uzen 21.1 pct 56 C; Kumkol 14.4 pct 50 C; Akshabulak 16.1 pct 53 C; Botakhan 3.1 pct 22 C; East Makhat 2.1 pct 16.67 C)
conditions: Askarova data, surface conditions
citation: Karazhanova, M.K., Kirisenko, O.G., Zhetekova, L.B., Smagulova, D.B. (2021). Statistical analysis and estimation of oil saturation by temperature paraffin. Azerbaijan Chemical Journal, 2021(3), 21-26.
notes: Five real oil points usable as checks; resins and asphaltenes also given.

subject: log10(wax content)
magnitude: WAT = 17.48 + 17.39 log10(wax wt%), r = 0.44, on 166 non-Algerian master_v9 rows
conditions: our own fit on the project dataset, mixed wax and WAT methods
citation: This study (fit on master_v9.csv).
notes: Benchmark: the Russian log-wax laws have the right shape but half the slope fits the mixed-method master data; wax alone explains only about 20 pct of WAT variance.

subject: paraffin content and paraffin/asphaltene ratio
magnitude: pour point vs paraffin content linear, R2 0.8093; vs paraffin/asphaltene ratio R2 0.897; vs paraffin/resin ratio R2 0.6949
conditions: 11 oils (10 West Siberia, 1 Volga-Ural); paraffin 3.5-22.0 wt%; pour point -12 to +17 C
citation: Yudina, N.V., Loskutova, Yu.V., Prozorova, I.V. (2023). Formation of asphalt-resin-paraffin deposits in oils of Western Siberia. Petroleomics, 3(1), 113-120.
notes: Equations only in figures; asphaltenes counteract wax (higher asphaltene at same paraffin gives lower pour point), so a generator should let pour point depend on paraffin/asphaltene, not paraffin alone.

subject: paraffin content
magnitude: pairwise correlation coefficient r = 0.6 between pour point and paraffin content
conditions: 350 Soviet (West Siberian) oil samples; correlation matrix
citation: Blagopoluchnaya, G.G., Smolyaninova, N.M. (1973). On relationships between some physico-chemical characteristics of oils. Izvestiya Tomskogo Politekhnicheskogo Instituta, 257.
notes: Large sample; paraffin explains only about 36 pct of pour point variance across many oils.

subject: predictive UNIQUAC model
magnitude: predicted minus measured WAT from -3 C (Hammami A-1 vs CPM) to +11 C (Erickson oil 6); +1.7 C for Hammami A-10; Daridon data uncertainty about 2 K
conditions: 13 Ronningsen crudes plus Erickson, Calange, Daridon and Hammami oils; n-paraffin distribution estimated from total wax content
citation: Coutinho, J.A.P., Edmonds, B., Moorwood, T., Szczepanski, R., Zhang, X. (2006). Reliable wax predictions for flow assurance. Energy and Fuels, 20(3), 1081-1088.
notes: Even a good thermodynamic model with measured wax content misses WAT by several C for some oils; sets an error floor for synthetic data from thermodynamics.

subject: kinematic viscosity and pour point
magnitude: regression model for wax content (acetone method) from kinematic viscosity and pour point: standard error of estimate 1.28 (wt%), R2 0.92
conditions: Indian crude oils (IIP Dehradun); wax by acetone precipitation; equation not seen
citation: Majhi, A., Sharma, Y.K., Kukreti, V.S., Bhatt, K.P., Khanna, R. (2015). Wax content of crude oil: a function of kinematic viscosity and pour point. Petroleum Science and Technology, 33(4), 381-387.
notes: Closed access; explicit equation exists in the paper and is a priority to read (it is the inverse of our WAT problem and links exactly our inputs). The abstract says it beat other existing wax content models.

subject: cloud point minus pour point
magnitude: cloud point exceeds pour point by 9 to 12 C (A 23/11, B 14/2, C 23/14, D 20/8 C); both rise with SG in figures
conditions: 4 Nigerian crude samples, SG 0.79-0.90; methods ASTM-type manual
citation: Eyankware, E.O., Ulakpa, W.C., Eyankware, M.O. (2016). Determination of cloud and pour point of crude oil with reference to crude transportation. International Journal of Science and Healthcare Research, 1(3).
notes: Small low-quality study; cloud point of dark crude by eye is unreliable. Use only as a weak prior.
